proposal.utterance: In BFO terms, what is an unjust command?

entities.label: Command
entities.rationale: A command is a normative content-bearer — an information artifact whose content (the directive) can be instantiated in multiple physical media (written orders, spoken utterances, encoded regulations). It is therefore a generically dependent continuant, analogous to Statute already in the ontology.

entities.label: UnjustCommand
entities.rationale: An unjust command is a subtype of Command that additionally bears a moral-defect quality. Its legal/normative existence (as a generically dependent continuant) is independent of its moral worth, consistent with working:LegalExistenceIndependenceFromMoralWorth already in the ontology.

entities.label: CommandIssuanceProcess
entities.rationale: A command comes into being through an issuance process — an occurrent in which an authorized agent (bearer of a role such as CourtAuthority) produces the command as output. This process is distinct from the command content itself.

entities.label: MoralDefectQuality
entities.rationale: The 'unjust' predicate in 'unjust command' denotes a quality that inheres in the command's bearer (the issuing institution or the command content as carried by a material document). It is a specifically dependent continuant of the quality sub-type, parallel to existing quality classes like InstitutionalPersistence and InstitutionalEffectiveness.

entities.label: AuthorityRole
entities.rationale: Commands are issued by agents bearing an authority role. This role class generalizes existing working:CourtAuthority and is needed to relate any command to its issuing role-bearer. Introducing it as a class avoids redundancy with the individual CourtAuthority already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: An unjust command is a species of command — it has all the ontological features of a command and additionally bears a moral-defect quality.
CourtAuthority is an existing role class that is a subtype of the more general AuthorityRole; making this explicit supports the relation between authority-bearers and commands.

The moral-defect quality inheres in the unjust command (its bearer). This encodes that unjustness is a specifically dependent continuant whose existence depends on the command that bears it, without affecting the command's legal existence as a generically dependent continuant.
The issuance process realizes the authority role of the issuing agent — the role is manifested through the act of commanding, consistent with BFO realized-in / realizes semantics.
Explicit superclass assertion placing Command under Generically dependent continuant in the hierarchy.

open_questions: Should 'Command' be restricted to legally issued commands (i.e., a subclass of a LegalNorm or Statute family), or should it cover any directive (military, parental, divine)?

Is the 'unjust' quality intended to be evaluated against natural-law criteria, positive-law criteria, or a separate moral standard? This affects whether MoralDefectQuality should subclass an existing working class such as LegalLegitimacyCondition or remain independent.

Do you want to distinguish between (a) a command that is unjust in content (e.g., orders an immoral act) and (b) a command that is unjust in origin (e.g., issued without legitimate authority)? These could be two sub-qualities or sub-classes.
Should CommandIssuanceProcess be linked to existing BehavioralLegalManifestation (already in the ontology as a Process subclass), or kept as a separate process type?

Is an 'unjust command' still legally valid/existent in your framework (positivist reading), or does injustice threaten its legal existence (natural-law reading)? This determines whether MoralDefectQuality co-inheres with or undermines LegalExistenceCondition.
proposal.rationale_summary: In BFO terms, a command is most naturally a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031): it is a normative information artifact whose content — the directive — can be concretized in many physical bearers (a written order, a spoken utterance, a statutory provision) but whose identity is tied to its content rather than any particular substrate, exactly as Statute is already typed in the working ontology. An unjust command is then a subclass of Command that additionally bears a MoralDefectQuality — a specifically dependent continuant (Quality, BFO_0000019) that inheres in the command. Crucially, following the principle already encoded in working:LegalExistenceIndependenceFromMoralWorth, the presence of this quality does not by itself annul the command's existence as a generically dependent continuant; it is an additional descriptor. The command comes into being through a CommandIssuanceProcess (Process, BFO_0000015) in which an agent bearing an AuthorityRole (Role, BFO_0000023) participates; that process realizes the authority role. This structure cleanly separates ontological existence conditions (what makes the command a command) from legitimacy conditions (what makes it just or unjust), mirroring the LegalExistenceCondition / LegalLegitimacyCondition distinction already present in the working ontology.
